skills: Year 1
Calculus and algebra technique fluent enough to think about the idea, not the manipulation (MAT 105 for APE and Physics; MAT 122 and MAT 123 for Mathematics).
Writing mathematics in full sentences - definitions, statements, proofs - from MAT 111 Principles of Mathematics onward.
A first programming language used on a real problem (CSE 101 or CSE 110; MAT 124 Scientific Programming for Mathematics).
Lab discipline from the first 1.5-credit lab (APE 104 or PHY 116): a data table with a unit and an uncertainty on every reading.
Year 2
Linear algebra and differential equations you can compute and explain (MAT 203 for APE and Physics; MAT 212 and MAT 222 for Mathematics).
Probability and statistics with intuition as well as formulas - STA 201 is core in all three programmes.

APE: circuits you can debug on the bench (APE 103, APE 203, APE 205). Physics: electricity, magnetism and optics derived from memory (PHY 115, PHY 202). Mathematics: first real proofs (MAT 221 Real Analysis I, MAT 311 Abstract Algebra).
A computer-algebra or numerical tool: MAT 250 Mathematics Lab I and MAT 223 Numerical Analysis I (Mathematics), MAT 205 Introduction to Numerical Methods (Physics core, APE elective).
Year 3
Numerical methods implemented, not just derived (MAT 205; MAT 312 Numerical Analysis II; ECE 328 Digital Signal Processing on a signal you recorded, for APE).

APE: a working analog build and a working digital build (APE 302, APE 204, the APE 301 lab). Physics: quantum mechanics I to III (PHY 303, 304, 305) and the modern-physics lab PHY 307. Mathematics: complex analysis and the second analysis course (MAT 314, MAT 321).
Reading a paper or a textbook chapter on your own and presenting it to classmates.
Electives chosen as a set that points one way - five for APE and Mathematics, four for Physics.
Year 4
A thesis or project with a clear question, method and result (APE 400, MAT 400, PHY 400) and a defence you have rehearsed in front of someone.
APE: the 1-credit internship at an R/D institution or an electronics and IT firm, with a report.
A portfolio: typeset notes or a proof portfolio (Mathematics); lab reports with uncertainty analysis (Physics); a working device or a measured circuit (APE).
Applications for jobs, scholarships or graduate programmes prepared a semester early.
dept.career_intro: Three degrees share this department, and they lead different places: APE toward electronics, instrumentation, telecom and IT; Mathematics toward analytics, finance, software, teaching and research; Physics toward research, medical and radiation physics, teaching and data work. Your electives and your thesis or project are the two loudest signals on your CV, so point them the same way. These are common directions, not BRACU rules.
careers: Electronics, instrumentation and embedded work (APE)
Designing, testing and maintaining circuits, instruments and small embedded systems.

APE 205 and APE 302 solid, APE 401 Measurements & Measuring Instruments, APE 404 Microprocessors and Assembly Language Programming, ECE 424 Power Electronics, the four APE labs and one device you built end to end.
Telecommunications and networks (APE)
Network planning, RF and link engineering with operators, vendors and ISPs.
ECE 310 and ECE 320 (core), ECE 330, ECE 430 Satellite Communications, CSE 421 Computer Networks, APE 406 Radar Engineering; a link you measured.
Data, analytics and software (all three)
Turning data into decisions, or building the software that does.

CSE 110 (GED for Mathematics and Physics; an outside-major option with CSE 111 for APE), MAT 124, CSE 220 and CSE 221 (Mathematics electives), STA 201, MAT 205; three projects with real data and written conclusions.
Banking, insurance and quantitative work (Mathematics)
Risk, pricing, forecasting and operations research.
STA 201, STA 301 Modern Probability Theory & Stochastic Processes, MAT 316 and MAT 424 Operations Research, MAT 423 Mathematical Modeling; spreadsheets and one language.
Medical and radiation physics (Physics, APE)
Hospitals, radiotherapy and imaging, radiation safety.
PHY 406 Medical Physics and Instrumentation, PHY 409 Physics of Radiology, PHY 416 Radiation Biophysics (Physics); the department page names an MS in Medical Physics starting from Fall 2026.
Energy, earth and atmosphere (APE, Physics)
Power and renewable-energy firms, meteorological and geophysical services.
APE 407 The Physics of Energy, APE 402 Plasma Physics with Industrial Applications; PHY 402 Atmospheric Physics, PHY 411 Geophysics, PHY 412 Dynamical and Tropical Meteorology.
Teaching
Schools, colleges, coaching and - with further degrees - universities.
Depth in the core courses, a tutoring record, the habit of explaining a derivation on a board.
Research and higher study
A master's and PhD in mathematics, physics, electronics or a neighbouring field.
CGPA, a serious thesis (APE 400, MAT 400 or PHY 400), the theory electives (PHY 408, PHY 413, PHY 414; MAT 411, MAT 422), a paper or poster, two recommenders who supervised your work.
Government service and the public sector
General and technical cadres filled through public recruitment examinations.
Broad preparation alongside the degree; the core kept fresh.

programs.version_note: This is the only APE curriculum printed on bracu.ac.bd; the programme page carries no version label or date beyond "This program started in Fall, 2009" and warns that "the courses listed below may change as the need be in future". All 130 credits are itemised: General Education 21, Departmental Core Courses 57, Elective Courses 15, Lab 6, Thesis/Project and Internship 4 (APE 400 3 credits + Internship 1 credit), Courses Outside Major Specialization 27, and every course carries its credits in the Course Details tab. The 1-credit Internship is printed with no course code, so it is one blank row for you to fill from your advising sheet. The page prints no number of elective or outside-major courses (15 and 27 credits only), no duration in years and no semester-by-semester plan: the 12 semesters here are the planner's 4 years x 3 semesters default, while the page itself places the thesis/project "in the 7th and 8th semester". If your advising sheet differs, it wins.
facts: "The total credit requirement for BS in APE degree is 130": General Education 21 + Departmental Core Courses 57 + Elective Courses 15 + Lab 6 + Thesis/Project and Internship 4 + Courses Outside Major Specialization 27 (the page prints credit totals per heading, not course counts).

Thesis/project: "A student is required to carry out thesis/project work in the 7th and 8th semester in a chosen field."; the supervisor is "a BRAC University faculty or any other suitable expert"; on completion the student submits "the dissertation/report" and must "face a viva board for the defence"; APE 400 Thesis/Project carries 3 credits.

Internship (1 credit, no course code printed): "The internship aims at providing on the job exposure to the students"; "Students will be placed at R/D institutions, electronics & IT firms etc for their internship programme."; no duration is printed.

Labs are four separate 1.5-credit courses - APE 104 APE Lab I, APE 206 APE Lab II, APE 301 APE Lab III, APE 303 APE Lab IV (6 credits); APE 405 "includes a compulsory 3 hour laboratory work each week" and CSE 421 "a compulsory 3 hour laboratory work alternate week".

ENG 091 Foundation Course is listed under General Education as "(non-credit)"; the Freshman Enrollment page says the admission test result prescribes one or more of ENG 091, MAT 091 and MAT 092 (non-credit) before ENG 101 and ENG 102 (3 credits each), and "If a freshman is prescribed two (02) non-credit courses, the third course for him/her is optional."
Electives: 15 credits from the 24 listed courses, all 3 credits (five courses); the page does not print how many.

Courses Outside Major Specialization: 27 credits from the 19 listed courses (ARC 292 Painting and ARC 293 Music Appreciation are 2 credits each, the rest 3) - "Other courses may also be taken from the approved courses of BU with the permission of the student's advisor and the Chair of the relevant Department."

"Options for doing a double- major with another major or a minor in APE are also available." - no credit figure or course list for an APE minor or double major is printed anywhere read (the department's Minor and Double Major pages cover Mathematics and Physics only).
PHY 310 Advanced Solid State Physics and PHY 311 X-Rays are printed with "Prerequisite APE 201" on this page (the Physics programme page prints PHY 201 for the same codes).

Credit load (Policies and Procedures page, university-wide): a freshman takes "maximum of nine (9) credits/ three (3) courses" unless authorised otherwise; from the second semester a minimum of 9 and a maximum of 15 credits, with 18 or more only in special cases with approvals.

University rules (Policies and Procedures page): graduation needs a minimum CGPA of 2.00 and at least 70 of the credits earned at BRAC University; from Summer 2022 a CGPA below 2.0 means probation with 3 consecutive semesters to recover; the degree must be finished within 8 years of first admission; "Attending Residential semester is compulsory for all BRAC University students."; attendance of 70% (90% for laboratory sessions) is needed to sit the final.

Admission (Undergraduate Admission page): SSC/equivalent and HSC/equivalent minimum GPA 3.5 (O-Levels 2.5 in five subjects, A-Levels 2.5 in two); APE needs an HSC/equivalent "B" grade in Physics & Mathematics or an A-level "C" grade in Physics & Mathematics, or IB-DP with a minimum DP score of 24; the admission test is "English (Composition and MCQ), Mathematics MCQ, Higher Mathematics MCQ and Physics MCQ".

Fees (Tuition and Fees page, undergraduate fees for new students enrolled from Spring 2027): tuition Tk. 8,250 per credit and semester fee Tk. 10,520 ("All other Program" row - APE is not named), admission fee Tk. 33,900 (one time), library membership fee Tk. 2,500 (one time), application fee Tk. 1,750; "Fees can be changed as per the decision of the university."

Three semesters a year - "There are three equal semesters-Spring, Fall, and Summer", each "13 working weeks" plus a final-exam week (Policies and Procedures page; the Academic Dates page shows Spring, Summer and Fall 2026).

small: Programme structures, rules, fees and dates checked against BRAC University's official web pages (bracu.ac.bd) in October 2026.
Independent, unofficial study product. Not produced by, affiliated with or endorsed by BRAC University. Always confirm with the Office of the Registrar, your advisor and your department.

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole MPS degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Science in Applied Physics and Electronics, Bachelor of Science in Mathematics, Bachelor of Science in Physics as BRACU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on BRACU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - BRACU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official BRACU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from BRACU's own web pages on 20 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Your data

Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from BRAC University's published pages as they stood in October 2026; the source is named under each section.
The grading scale
BRAC University's undergraduate scale, in force since Fall 2020. Both A+ and A carry the full 4.0.
A+ to D- are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA. The policy page prints the same formula: the sum of (grade points x credits) over the credits attempted.
Three things students get wrong

items: **An F stays in the sum until it is retaken.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top.
**A D- passes, but it costs you.** A 3-credit D- is 2.1 quality points against 12.0 for an A - and a grade of B- or below is what the repeat rule exists for.
**W, I, P and AU never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.
